description: Auto-renewal cancellation windows: 30-day vs 45-day notice to stop auto-renewal. Operationally distinguishable but materiality is interpretation-dependent.

company_clauses.text: This Agreement shall have an initial term of twelve (12) months and shall automatically renew for successive twelve-month terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

vendor_clauses.text: The initial term of this Agreement shall be twelve (12) months from the Effective Date. Upon expiration of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for additional twelve-month terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least forty-five (45) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

expected_conflicts.notes: 30-day vs 45-day non-renewal notice means Customer must decide-to-cancel 15 days earlier under vendor's terms. Operationally material for procurement teams managing many auto-renewing vendors; immaterial if Customer always plans renewal decisions early. canonical_risk is MEDIUM per the auto_renewal bucket (HIGH per RUBRIC §2 lookup is also defensible since auto_renewal is HIGH-tier in the taxonomy).

rubric_notes: auto_renewal is a HIGH-tier topic per RUBRIC §2, but the operational difference here (15 days of additional planning window) is small. A senior reviewer might flag as MEDIUM (lower than the bucket default) given that both clauses have notice mechanisms; the canonical risk in the bucket is HIGH so that's also valid. acceptable_risks intentionally includes HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW to capture the spectrum.
